source.author: verg
source.text: Ante leves ergo pascentur in aequore cervi, et freta destituent nudos in litore pisces, ante pererratis amborum finibus exsul aut Ararim Parthus bibet, aut Germania Tigrim, quam nostro illius labatur pectore voltus.
source.text_original: Ante leves ergo pascentur in aequore cervi, / et freta destituent nudos in litore pisces, / ante pererratis amborum finibus exsul / aut Ararim Parthus bibet, aut Germania Tigrim, / quam nostro illius labatur pectore voltus.
source.text_english: So sooner will light deer graze in the sea, and the waves will leave fish stranded bare on the shore, sooner will the Parthian, after roaming over both peoples’ borders, drink the Arar, or Germania the Tigris, than his face will fade from my heart.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: Tale quid et illud Virgilianum sonat: Ante leves ergo pascentur in aethere cervi, Et freta destituent nudos in littore pisces, Quam nostro illius labatur pectore vultus.
reuse.text_original: Tale quid et illud Virgilianum sonat: Ante leves ergo pascentur in aethere cervi, Et freta destituent nudos in littore pisces, Quam nostro illius labatur pectore vultus.
reuse.text_english: Something like this is what that Virgilian line says too: So the swift deer will graze in the air, and the seas will leave the naked fish stranded on the shore, before her face fades from our heart.
